svg.aria-label: Memory budget of the reference Atlas cluster. Of about 42 GiB allocatable across three 16 GB nodes, the lean baseline stack uses 12 to 14 GiB and the worst case with everything scaled at once reaches about 25 GiB, leaving headroom. The second bar shows that at 16 GB the binding limit becomes the pod cap, not memory.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
text.tspan: · memory is the ceiling, not CPU

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Under load the app tier peaks well within its CPU limits but close to its memory requests — so size for RAM first, then check the pod cap.

svg.text: The lean stack is apps + CNPG + one Kafka broker + Keycloak + the LGTM stack. The peak adds HPA scale-up, a 3-broker Kafka, a CNPG replica and Tempo.

svg.text: 42 of 45 — three pods of headroom. Raise max-pods-per-node to ~30 during the node recycle: it is a scheduling ceiling, so it costs no compute.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Even the worst case fits in 42 GiB with ~17 GiB to spare. 24 GB nodes would just be idle, paid-for RAM — and the pod cap, not memory, is what binds first.
